notes: Four-lane parallel sweep (ai / bigtech+hardware+mobile / devtools+cloud / security) via background subagents, covering 2026-10-03 and 2026-10-04. All lanes hit routine EGRESS_BLOCKED on most org-domain WebFetch attempts and worked from WebSearch snippets quoting those pages instead (anthropic.com/news was fetched directly in the AI lane with nothing new past Oct 2). Highlights: Trump's new White House 'Super Intelligence Force' AI task force and a US-China AI-incident hotline agreement (both genuinely dated Oct 3-4), California's SB 947 'No Robo Bosses Act' effective date, a new Citrix NetScaler KEV deadline and an Oracle quarterly CPU date, plus several precision/sourcing corrections to already-filed hardware and devtools entries (NVIDIA RTX Spark, Intel 14A PDK, TypeScript 7.1, Apple's rumored Oct 13 event, Samsung Unpacked 2027). Dropped several near-duplicate candidates where lane agents re-found something already on the calendar (Googlebook, three CISA KEV deadlines already at day precision, Azure DevOps OIDC issuer retirement, Kubernetes 1.36 EOL, Apple App Store SDK requirement) rather than file a no-op or risk a fuzzy-match miss creating a duplicate row.
concerns: Google Cloud Next 2027 (Apr 13-15, Mandalay Bay) is unresolved for a 4th straight run: every source is a templated third-party event-aggregator site (gracker.ai, egen.ai, 10times, beri.net, etc.) with zero citation of cloud.google.com, blog.google or press — looks like unverified SEO content rather than a real leak, so still not filed even at 'expected'. A maintainer with unblocked access to cloud.google.com/next should settle this directly.

Found two conflicting 'expected' earnings-date estimates for Amazon Q3 2026 (calendar currently has Oct 22 from TipRanks; a fresh MarketBeat search this run returned Oct 29) and for Alphabet Q3 2026 (calendar has Oct 28; a fresh WallStreetHorizon-adjacent search returned Oct 27). Neither is sourced to the company itself, and the merge logic lets an incoming date silently overwrite the existing one, so deliberately did NOT file either correction rather than flip a coin between two guesses. Worth watching for the companies' own IR press releases, which usually land ~2 weeks prior.

Pre-existing duplicate in data/events/2026-10.json: 'Azure retires Anomaly Detector, Metrics Advisor and Personalizer' and 'Azure retires Personalizer, Anomaly Detector and Metrics Advisor' are the same Oct 1 2026 event filed twice under reordered titles (token-overlap dedupe in src/lib/id.ts apparently fell just under the 0.6 threshold). Not something this run can fix (no hand-editing data/), flagging for a maintainer to merge/delete one.

Found a real id.ts dedupe false-positive, not just a near-miss: a genuinely new 'GitHub Enterprise Server 3.18 reaches end of life' finding (confirmed via docs.github.com/en/enterprise-server@3.18/admin/release-notes, Oct 14 2026) fuzzy-matched onto the already-filed 3.17 entry ('GitHub Enterprise Server 3.17 reaches end of life', Sept 22 2026) in a --dry-run — same org, >=0.6 title-token overlap since only the version digit differs, and well within the 75-day event-drift window. Applying it would have silently overwritten/lost the 3.17 entry instead of adding a new 3.18 one, so it was dropped from this run rather than filed. This looks like a structural gap in src/lib/id.ts's isSameThing: any 'Product X.N reaches end of life/support' pair for sequential versions is at risk of colliding, since the version number is only one token out of several shared ones. A maintainer should consider weighting the version-number token specially (or requiring exact match on any token that looks like a version number) before this trips on a real pair of versions again.

Several corrections this run had to reuse an existing entry's exact title text to force a dedupe match that the token-overlap algorithm (src/lib/id.ts isSameThing, 0.6 Jaccard floor) would otherwise miss — e.g. 'TypeScript 7.1 expected to restore stable programmatic API' kept verbatim even though the new finding is really about a firmer release date, and 'Apple expected to unveil new smart home hub, HomePod mini and Apple TV 4K' kept verbatim despite the HomePad product name surfacing. Same standing issue flagged in prior runs' concerns about src/lib/id.ts token collisions, just hitting from the opposite direction (near-misses that would have duplicated, not merged).

Low-credibility scraper sites (senserva.com, trinetriops.com) claim Microsoft's Oct 13 2026 Patch Tuesday will ship only 1 CVE with zero exploited zero-days; unverifiable against msrc.microsoft.com (blocked) and suspicious for a future date, so not filed — worth a direct MSRC check closer to Oct 13.

A Symantec/Broadcom report on China-nexus 'Warlock' ransomware (water utility, telecom, government body, university via SharePoint flaws) has a vendor bulletin dated Oct 1, 2026, outside this run's Oct 3-4 announcement window, even though secondary outlets republished it Oct 3. Left out per the no-backfill rule; flagging in case the team wants republish dates treated differently.
